newsitem.title: UK: Bass declines comment on Accor talk.
newsitem.headline: Bass declines comment on Accor talk.

text.p: Brewing and leisure group Bass Plc declined to comment on market rumours that it was planning to bid for French hotels group Accor.
"We never comment on market speculation," said a spokeswoman for Bass.
Accor shares were up four percent in Paris at 733 francs and Bass shares were off 4p at 857p on the rumours, dealers said.

"I can see the initial logic in the idea, because it would fill a geographic hole that Bass has in Europe but there are a number of problems associated with ownership of properties and overlap of brands," said Nikko analyst Dermott Carr.
"There are also a range of complex put options between Accor and a number of French institutions which would complicate the deal significantly," he added.
Many analysts said it looks like a homespun rumour designed to whip up some enthusiasm for the stock, but they acknowledge Bass is cash rich and keen to expand its hotel business.
Analysts also estimate Accor, with a market capitalisation of 23 billion francs and net debt of 17 billion francs, is worth about $4 billion.

The company owns 2,378 hotels, making it the fifth largest hotel chain in the world. About half its hotels are in Europe and include the mid-ranking Ibis, Novotel and Mercure brand as well as the premier Sofitel name. It also owns budget hotels Formula One in Europe and Motel Six in North America. Aside from hotels, Accor owns a luncheon vouchers business, a travel agency and an institutional catering business through a 21.6 percent shareholding in Britain's Compass.
